text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.4% today after climbing sharply over the past two days, as crude oil prices pulled back and incoming diesel supplies threatened to ease the tight market that had been driving refiner margins higher. The International Energy Agency announced plans to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel, which directly undercuts the supply shortage that has kept diesel prices elevated—a key source of profit for refiners like Marathon. At the same time, U.S. crude slipped as traders digested these supply developments, even as geopolitical risks in the Middle East remain present.

The stock's two-week surge of 12.6% had been built on climbing oil prices and the tight diesel situation, but today's news that major supplies are coming to market represents a real shift in the near-term outlook for refinery profits. Refineries running at 92.7% capacity—near their typical high—now face the prospect of wider supply availability, which historically compresses the margin between crude costs and refined product sales that makes the refining business profitable.
